LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. The Packers won three games in a row after a 1-2 start, and they welcomed back veteran running back Josh Jacobs in Week 7 after he was suspended for the first six games of the campaign. Now, the Packers find themselves as favorites at home against a Carolina team that is just 3-3 in the 2026 season after a blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Tampa Bay ran all over Carolina's defense, allowing over five yards per carry this season. And Bryce Young and company are looking to prove that they are an actual playoff contender after winning the division in the 2025 season. Carolina's offense has been pretty good through six games, with Young throwing for a ton of yardage to lead the team to a 3-3 start. But a shaky showing out of the bye in Week 6 certainly puts some pressure on the Panthers as they look to fend off the Atlanta Falcons and the Bucs in the NFC South. Oddsmakers have set the Packers as favorites in this matchup, and Green Bay needs every win it can get to compete in a division where all four teams are currently over .500. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. Credit: AP/Nick Wass CHARLOTTE, N.C. — The Baltimore Ravens have added another offensive playmaker for quarterback Lamar Jackson. The Ravens acquired wide receiver Diontae Johnson and a sixth-round pick in 2025 on Tuesday from the Carolina Panthers for a 2025 fifth-rounder. The Panthers announced the terms of the trade late Tuesday. Johnson had been Carolina’s leading wide receiver since being acquired in an offseason trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers for cornerback Donte Jackson. Johnson has 30 receptions for 357 yards and three touchdowns for Carolina, but did not play in Sunday’s 28-14 loss to the Denver Broncos because of a rib injury. Johnson was set to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. According to a person familiar with the trade, two other teams expressed interest in acquiring Johnson before the Ravens got involved a couple of days ago. Given the compensation for Johnson, it’s likely that some teams were scared off by his past issues in the locker room. Eager to improve their draft positioning for next season, the Panthers are likely to listen to more calls before the Nov. 5 trade deadline. Carolina Panthers wide receiver Diontae Johnson (5) celebrates a touchdown in the first half of an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons in Charlotte, N.C., Sunday, Oct. 13, 2024. Credit: AP/Jacob Kupferman One player that would make sense to move is running back Miles Sanders, but it's unclear if he would command anything on the trade market given his lack of production for Carolina over the past season-and-a-half. Despite their 1-7 record, the Panthers appear unlikely to trade some players, including quarterback Bryce Young, running back Chuba Hubbard and cornerback Jaycee Horn. Hubbard and Horn are well-liked by the organization and could be in line for contract extensions. Jackson, a two-time MVP, is having the best passing season of his career for the Ravens, with a 115.4 rating and 2,099 yards. He’s thrown 17 touchdown passes with only two interceptions. Johnson joins second-year wide receiver Zay Flowers and 24-year-old Rashod Bateman — plus a handful of capable tight ends — among Jackson’s options. Watson was able to return from the hospital and play, notching a couple of receptions in the second half, including one that helped seal the Packers' victory. Meanwhile, the Panthers dropped to 3-4 with their loss and could lose their perch atop the NFC South if the Atlanta Falcons beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week. Christian Watson made one of the most remarkable returns to a game ever . When Watson suffered a chest injury in the first half, it looked like his night was over. The downfield threat was taken via ambulance to a local hospital for precautionary testing, and many were worried he had suffered a serious injury. Instead, Watson ended up being OK. He returned to the stadium in the ambulance, took the field in the second half, and even made a couple of catches. His return was a combination of shocking and remarkable The Packers' running game remains a significant problem . Josh Jacobs' return has provided the Packers with a small boost out of the backfield, but the team still struggled to run the ball against a Panthers defense that has been weak against the run. Green Bay's issues running the ball particularly showed up in the fourth quarter, when they weren't able to sustain drives on the ground to milk their 14-point lead over Carolina. The Packers will continue to struggle to close out games as long as they can't run the ball, so Matt LaFleur needs to fix it quickly as Green Bay looks to make a playoff push. Watson returned to the game in the second half after leaving Lambeau Field in an ambulance. “One of the doctors had his phone out, I was just watching the play-by-play,” Watson told Kaylee Hartung how he was following the game on the way to the hospital. The bad news for the Packers? Watson suffered a chest injury after a 53-yard catch and had to be taken to the hospital as a result . Green Bay hasn't officially ruled him out, but the Packers will presumably be without him as they look to close out a home win against Carolina. The Green Bay Packers announced Watson is "questionable" to return to Thursday's game because of a chest injury. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Baltimore enters Week 8 at 4-3 after consecutive losses to Cleveland and Cincinnati, while quarterback Lamar Jackson is expected to return after missing three games with a high ankle sprain. Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring at 32.8 points per game and ranks fourth in total offense at 387.7 yards per contest. The Ravens must win several important individual matchups to keep the Bills from controlling the game. 1. Cam Jurgens and Baltimore's interior offensive line vs. Buffalo's defensive tackles Baltimore needs improved execution from its interior offensive line after Derrick Henry managed just 45 yards against Cincinnati. Jurgens, acquired earlier this season, must help organize blocking assignments against Buffalo's defensive front. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane returned to practice Thursday and Friday after a knee injury, though his availability still needs monitoring. Buffalo defensive tackle Ed Oliver has also been managing an injury. His status could affect how the Bills rotate players inside. 2. Derrick Henry vs. Buffalo's run defense Henry enters the matchup with 579 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, but Baltimore needs more consistent gains on early downs. Buffalo's defensive front must stop Henry from building momentum through the interior, especially when the Ravens use heavier formations. Jackson's expected return should create additional decisions for the Bills' linebackers and defensive ends, potentially giving Henry more favorable rushing lanes. 3. Josh Allen vs. Roquan Smith and Kyle Hamilton Allen enters Week 8 needing 39 rushing yards to reach 5,000 for his career. He also has eight rushing touchdowns this season, creating another challenge for Baltimore's defense near the goal line. Smith and Hamilton returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session with knee injuries. Their availability and ability to recognize quarterback runs will be essential to limiting Allen's production outside the pocket. 4. Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey vs. Buffalo's receivers Allen's ability to extend plays places additional pressure on opposing cornerbacks, who must maintain coverage after the initial route combinations break down. Wiggins and Humphrey will have difficult assignments against Buffalo's receiving group, including Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and Joshua Palmer. Baltimore needs its secondary to avoid coverage breakdowns, particularly after allowing five consecutive second-half touchdown possessions against Cincinnati. 5. Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green vs. Buffalo's offensive tackles Baltimore has recorded 16 sacks through seven games, but pressuring Allen requires more than simply reaching the backfield. Hendrickson and Green must maintain containment while forcing Allen to make decisions from inside the pocket. Buffalo tackle Spencer Brown missed Thursday's practice with a back injury, creating another situation worth monitoring before kickoff. Final analysis The Ravens cannot afford to sacrifice rush discipline in pursuit of sacks. Keeping Allen contained while maintaining coverage integrity could determine whether Baltimore ends its losing streak. away.blurb: Doyle added: “I think that you have to be very aware of any — you take a guy out of that flow that he was in, you have to be very aware of that. He hasn’t played football in a little bit. So, we’re trying to make the practice as close to game-like reps as we possibly can. … The goal is that you don’t skip a beat when he steps back out there, and that he’s able to continue to operate at the level he was in.” On paper, Allen can slice the Ravens’ secondary like a knife through hot butter. Next Gen Stats says watch out for the play action. That’s where the Ravens might trip him up. Allen’s 10.1 yards per attempt on play-action rank second in the NFL, while the Ravens are tied for the lowest rate against such misdirection (38.2%), along with a league-best 4.3 yards per attempt. Throughout October, we’ve seen a Ravens offense that is lights out on its opening drives, then sputters out and never really gets going again. Is that because Doyle scripts out his first few drives, then struggles to adjust as the game wears on? “I script out basically, ‘Here are my normal down-and-distance,’ which would be first-and-10 or second-and-6 or less, and then, ‘Here are my G-BOT [Get Back on Track] plays that I want to show first,’ which are basically second-and-7-to-10, second-and-11-plus, those things that are a little bit further distance. So, you try to make sure that in each of those areas, you’re studying the defense and what shows up accordingly, and that’s kind of what you want to just make sure your players understand: ‘When we get in this game, when we’re in these different situations, here’s what I’m thinking, here’s why I’m calling it.’” The Ravens locker room “confronted” a lot this week. Not in a “confrontational” way, safety Kyle Hamilton said, but they seem to understand they can’t just move on after a division rival stormed into Baltimore and hung 35 unanswered points. “Very real, grown-man conversations were had,” Hamilton said. “I think it was a point last week where that needed to be had.” This week has centered around leadership and resiliency, as much as it has the AFC foe next on the schedule. away.blurb: Lamar Jackson is nearing a return to the field. Jackson is on track to return in Week 8. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback turned in another full practice on Friday, Oct. 30, putting him on track to play against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Jackson has been sidelined for the last three games with an ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday, Oct. 26 that he thought Jackson would be in a decent spot to play this week, telling reporters, "If he's able to play … he will play." away.blurb: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady said Friday that five players will be questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens. WR DJ Moore (shoulder), TE Dalton Kincaid (chest), CB Dee Alford (ankle), DL Greg Gaines and RT Spencer Brown (back) will all carry a questionable designation tag for Week 8. Per Brady, Gaines "tweaked the lower body" during Friday's practice. Moore and Kincaid have been in red non-contact jerseys throughout the week of practice and have been "limited" on the team's injury report. "He's played a lot of football and man, he's playing at such a high level right now," Brady said. "I have a lot of trust in his preparation and not being able to get reps and still be able to go out there and do his job." Buffalo Bills right tackle Spencer Brown has been dealing with a back injury since he played the Los Angeles Rams on October 12. Click for sound 0:00 / 0:00 Brown left that 37-34 overtime win in Inglewood, California. He returned for Buffalo's 33-30 win in Las Vegas six days later. Pro Football Talk reports he said the back issue would not keep him off the field. He also explained how he got through the Rams game. Brown told reporters he "took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant when I was in LA." PFT notes that reporters chuckled, but Brown called it routine. "Everybody's laughing. It's protocol. NFL signed off on it, so it's OK," he said. "But yeah, just took care of the body the best way I knew how and got through the Vegas game and played pretty well and got on the bye week and kind of bit me in the butt a little bit. So, just taking it easy and smart." He added that the bye week "kind of bit me in the butt a little bit." Brown now says he is "taking it easy and smart." Get notified of the most viral NFL stories via Google! Brown insisted he still wants to play whenever he can. "I do pride myself on being ready every single day," he remarked. PFT's Michael David Smith wrote that it is fair to question whether the NFL should let players take the field when they need that kind of medication. He pointed to recent scrutiny, including Jalen Hurts' medical timeline . Smith also cited Christian Watson's trip to the hospital before the Packers receiver returned to Thursday night's game. Last week, the Bills did not play entirely because it was the team's bye. Prior to that, Brown had been dealing with a back injury and has missed practice twice this week ahead of facing the Ravens . picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup Patrick Judis Fri, October 30, 2026 at 8:08 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL world was shaken on Thursday morning when the Tennessee Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going in opposite directions. Tennessee is 1-6, and their offense is struggling to gel together around quarterback Cam Ward. Meanwhile, Cincinnati just took off like a jet last week, scoring 35 unanswered against the Baltimore Ravens. It seems pretty clear-cut how this game is expected to play out, but how do oddsmakers and experts feel about it? The Bengals are currently 11.5-point favorites against the Titans, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the biggest spread Cincinnati has had this season. They were only 6.5-point favorites against the Miami Dolphins coming off two straight losses. Safe to say the number got a little bigger after Tennessee traded Simmons this week. The point total is set at 46.5 points combined. The real wild card for these bets is which Bengals' defense is going to show up. Are they going to give up 200 rushing yards, or will they be able to shut it down like last week against Derrick Henry? All of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has a consensus of Cincinnati winning from their six experts None of NFL.com's five experts are taking the Titans NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick Initially, I was worried this may be a trap game at home for the Bengals. Sometimes this team will just drop a terrible game after a huge win. That happens especially when they are playing down to a bad team's level. I'm not sure how the Simmons trade might impact that, but I am hopeful the Titans are a bit more deflated coming out than fighting even harder. Either way, Burrow and this offense shouldn't have any trouble scoring and moving the ball. Their job got a lot easier without Simmons in the middle of that defense. The only thing I'm worried about offensively with the Titans is their running backs breaking off a few big runs. Bengals 41, Titans 13 Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jimmy Morris Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:21 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Each week I write a preview post on Fridays. Earlier in the week, I was thinking about the mismatch that the Cincinnati Bengals offense poses for the Tennessee Titans defense. That was when Jeffery Simmons was still on the Titans. Now that Big Jeff has been traded to the Chicago Bears, that mismatch is astronomical. Joe Burrow and the Bengals are 5th in the league in passing and 4th in the league in points scored per game. The Titans are 26th in the league against the pass. With Simmons in the middle of the defense, there was at least some hope that the Titans could create enough pressure to keep Burrow from having a career-type day. How are the Titans going to do that now? They aren't. The Simmons trade should open up snaps for Femi Oledajo and Keldric Faulk on the defensive lines. They are two young players that the Titans spent high draft picks on in hopes of them being able to disrupt the quarterback. We haven't seen that from either of those guys to this point. It is time for them to step up. If the Titans are going to have a chance to win this game, they are going to have to be able to keep pace with the Bengals offense. The Bengals pass defense hasn't been very good allowing 233 yards per game. Cam Ward has probably heard people talking this week about how the Simmons trade means they have given up on him. If he wants to quiet that talk, he needs to come out and have a big day against a pretty soft defense. The Titans opened as 10.5-point underdogs at FanDuel . That number moved to +11.5 when the trade was announced yesterday. I just don't see a way where they are going to be able to cover, much less win this game. Cincinnati (4-2) has won two straight, scoring all 35 of its points after halftime in a 35-13 win in Baltimore . Tennessee (1-6) lost 27-24 to Cleveland on a late kick. On Wednesday, Zac Taylor warned about Jeffery Simmons, "If you're not planning for him, you'll have some problems." On Thursday, the Titans sent Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks. He leads Cincinnati with 571 receiving yards, 220 more than Ja'Marr Chase, who was a full participant Thursday after a rest day. Tennessee has allowed only six touchdown passes, tied for third-fewest in the league. Opponents also complete 69.2% of their throws against the Titans, the second-highest rate in the NFL, so the yardage is there even when the end zone isn't. Joe Burrow carries PFF's top passing grade at 89.5 into Sunday, and we already looked at how his hot streak puts that touchdown number at risk. That's been the season in Nashville. Now the 1-6 Titans go to Cincinnati on Sunday a few days after trading Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks. Head coach Robert Saleh was blunt about why the calls came in. "Like I told our guys, when you don't close out games and you are standing here at 1-6, teams are going to start fishing," he said, per the team's website . Safety Amani Hooker said he "definitely was surprised and shocked" by the deal, per The Tennessean . Cincinnati (4-2) is a double-digit favorite , and Cam Ward needs a strong showing before the bye. Here are three bold predictions for a team that has lost four one-score games. Tony Pollard runs for 100 yards again Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) runs with the ball as New York Giants defensive lineman Shelby Harris (93) defends during a game at MetLife Stadium, Sep 27, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. Pollard has 478 yards and four touchdowns on 112 carries, and he forced 13 missed tackles before the Browns game, according to PFF . We looked at whether the Titans' run game is real after Cleveland, and Cincinnati's defense gives him another chance to prove it. The Bengals allow 4.7 yards per carry, per ESPN , and 116.3 rushing yards per game, 19th in the league, per The Associated Press . Linebacker Barrett Carter has missed eight tackles, according to PFF , and safety Kyle Dugger didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday with a quad injury. With Tyjae Spears sitting out both days with a knee injury, Pollard should get every carry he can handle. Bold prediction: Pollard goes over 100 rushing yards for the second straight week. away.headline: Kyle Dugger is out for the Bengals against the Titans as Budda Baker trade talk lingers
away.blurb: Kyle Dugger won’t play Sunday. The Cincinnati Bengals ruled out the veteran safety with a quadriceps injury for the home game against Tennessee, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is questionable, according to the team’s final injury report . The matchup is forgiving either way. The Bengals out-rank the Titans in all 12 EPA and success-rate categories , and Tennessee will be without receiver Carnell Tate, running back Tyjae Spears and punter Tommy Townsend at Paycor Stadium. Andrei Iosivas Eyeing Mid-November Return for Bengals Following Thumb Surgery That’s the entire list. Every other Bengal is healthy enough to go without a designation, which is about as clean as a Week 8 report gets. Cincinnati is 4-2 and coming off a 35-0 second half in Baltimore , so the timing could be a lot worse. A defense that just held Baltimore scoreless for 30 minutes doesn’t have to reshuffle much. Bengals’ safeties without Kyle Dugger Dugger has been a rotational piece more than a fixture, appearing in four of six games. Jordan Battle leads the team with three interceptions, and Bryan Cook has a forced fumble in five games. Russ Yeast and PJ Jules are the depth behind them. The position is still a talking point before the Nov. 10 deadline. Cincinnati has been tied to Budda Baker in trade rumors , and a lingering quad injury for Dugger would only add to that conversation. Giles-Harris matters for a different reason. He has played a reserve role, but the Bengals are thin enough at linebacker that we’ve already looked at three bold trades to add help there. Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter are the starters, and Oren Burks would pick up any extra snaps. Sunday is also the start of what looks like the NFL’s easiest remaining schedule . With Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins all off the report, the Bengals get to open that stretch close to full strength. away.headline: Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News
away.blurb: The team revealed several absences , with wide receiver Carnell Tate being officially ruled out with a shoulder injury. Cam Ward loses his top target and the Titans offense, which has struggled mightily to score, is facing a tough task against a surging Bengals team. Carnell Tate Officially Out in Week 8 There is really no reason to have Tate on the field unless he is playing at or near 100%. The Titans are already 1-6 and the team has a bye week following the Bengals game. This extra rest should mean Tate is ready to return in Week 10 and look to form some sort of connection with Ward before the season ends. If they cannot do so, or even if they can, Tate may be catching passes from a new quarterback in 2027. Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News Unlock the latest Heavy on Titans news — direct to your inbox. The Tennessee Titans need all hands on deck to have a chance to take down the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. That is why the team's latest injury report is such a crushing blow. Tate has not yet lived up to the hype of being the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL Draft. However, he has done well given the lack of success from Ward in his role running the offense. The rookie has 34 receptions for 413 yards and one touchdown through seven games. For context, Ward only has four total touchdown passes on the season. The 34 connections make Tate his quarterback's top target and his absence will loom large Sunday in Cincinnati. Carnell Tate Tyjae Spears Tommy Townsend. Yet with or without Tate, the Titans are massive underdogs in the game. ESPN shared DraftKings' odds listing the Bengals as 12.5-point favorites. A 1-6 start is not what Robert Saleh and company had in mind at the start of the season. The team is fresh off back-to-back 3-14 seasons, and seems to be headed in that same direction once again. Ward's second season is not going well and the coaching staff refuses to sit him and let him learn. Thus, they are hoping he can play through his issues and improve to at least make the Titans offense a competitive one. Losing Tate for any amount of time makes even scoring touchdowns a tall task for this offense in 2026. The Titans have the second-worst record in football right now, better than only the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers . This puts both teams in a race to the bottom for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That would be an intriguing draft slot for both teams, as the Titans have Ward and the Chargers have Justin Herbert. Would either team take a quarterback? For now, Ward is hoping to shock the entire NFL world on Sunday with a big performance without his top target on the field. But after snapping a two-game skid on Monday night, the Dallas Cowboys are chomping at the bit to get back on the field. Dallas doesn't have to wait long, hosting the Arizona Cardinals as near-touchdown chalk Sunday afternoon. My Cardinals vs. Cowboys predictions like Dallas to ride the momentum of that MNF victory, especially the reawakening of this explosive offense. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Cardinals vs Cowboys prediction: Cowboys -6.5 The Dallas Cowboys broke out of a two-game funk in which the offense stalled out on third downs. Against Philadelphia, the Cowboys finished 9-for-14 on third/fourth downs and reclaimed their spot among the Top 5 attacks in Week 7. The Arizona Cardinals defense has been at the mercy of a very tough schedule, and it shows in its ratings (28th in EPA/play). While the offense was able to counter their opponents' scores earlier in the year, Arizona's attack is sputtering with the third-lowest points per play average over the last three contests. Dallas is more than happy turning this game into a track meet and thrives on the clean indoor surface at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott especially enjoys Jerry's World, with his career metrics spiking at home (103.4 rating at home vs. 92.8 on road). This is Dallas first "normal" home game since Week 2 (played TNF at home in Week 5), and I'm grabbing this Cowboys offense short of the key number of a touchdown. Cardinals vs Cowboys combo Arizona was in a similar shootout spot with Detroit a few weeks back and couldn't keep pace with an explosive offense. Dallas does the same here, pulling away with plenty of points in the second half. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a two-TD day in Week 7 and faces a Cardinals defense allowing the second most touchdowns to rival receivers. Michael Wilson needs to be more involved, and Mike LaFleur knows it. With Arizona playing from behind, plenty of passes come his way, and projections call for as many as 70 yards on Sunday. Lamb will rip through an Arizona secondary ranked among the worst in the land but also featuring plenty of bodies on the injury report in Week 8. The Cardinals run one of the highest rates of zone coverage, and Lamb is excellent at spotting seams in that defense. He's not only a downfield threat but also a catch-and-run weapon, exploiting an Arizona stop unit giving up the seventh most yards after the catch. The Cardinals have allowed 10 touchdowns to WRs (second most), and Lamb's TD forecasts for Week 8 all sit at 60% or higher, with some projections at 80%. away.headline: Cowboys defenders Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs added to injury report vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs was limited in a walkthrough practice with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was also a new addition to the injury report as he's dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited on Wednesday. FRISCO - The Cowboys added some new names to the injury report Wednesday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that there were a few players dealing with some minor injuries, but nothing significant. The Cowboys could also be on the verge of some players returning . Safety PJ Locke III (foot) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) were both full participants Wednesday. Locke was added to injured reserve after hurting his foot in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Liufau fractured his forearm in the preseason finale. The Cowboys created one roster spot earlier this week when they waived running back Emari Demercado. He was claimed by the Houston Texans on Wednesday. If the Cowboys activate both Locke and Liufau, they'll have to make one more roster move. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson, another player on injured reserve , was seen working in the rehabilitation group during practice. He's been on injured reserve since he suffered a hamstring injury in late September. His practice window hasn't been opened yet. Read this story on dallasnews.com

away.blurb: LaFleur was asked whether Love will be back to 100%, now that he is cleared to return to game action. “You say 100% — even though he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys, by Nov. 1 are truly at 100,” LaFleur said. “He's feeling as good as he can feel. So kinda go from there.” “We're never gonna put a guy out there that we don't think can obviously benefit the team, benefit the offense,” LaFleur said. “… He's out there for a reason and we expect him to go.” Given that Love was limited by his ankle injury over the next two weeks — and that the Cardinals shut him down to get him close to 100% — it seems likely that they want to get him close to that workload, at least as it pertains to snap share. The Cardinals also expect to have wide receiver Michael Wilson available against the Cowboys, as he deals with a ribs injury. He was limited in practice all week, donning a yellow non-contact jersey in all three sessions. Right tackle Elijah Wilkinson is likewise good to go after dealing with a knee injury earlier in the week. Cornerback Max Melton (knee) and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) also appear set to return after missing last week’s game. Defensive tackle Walter Nolen and right guard Jon Gaines are both out with ankle injuries, LaFleur said. And center Hjalte Froholdt suffered a “tweak” to his knee on Thursday, Oct. 29, according to LaFleur, imperiling his availability. If Froholdt is out, the Cardinals would slide guard Hayden Conner to center. They would then need to fill right guard with yet another backup. Josh Fryar, a tackle, appears to be the most likely option to slide inside, although Kingsley Eguakun is another option. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' Jeremiyah Love to make his return in Week 8
away.blurb: Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love returned to the practice field as a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday after missing the last two games with a lingering ankle injury. Jeremiyah Love to make his return "Even though he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys are 100 percent," Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFluer said via Bo Brack, Arizona Cardinals reporter and host of the PHNX Cardinals Podcast. "He's feeling as good as he can feel; we'll go from there." Christian Watson details gritty return to Packers' 'TNF' win over Panthers after breaking rib, spitting up blood In five games this season, Love has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and one touchdown, adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined with the ankle injury. Love suffered a right high ankle sprain during the preseason on Aug. 13, during his debut against the Las Vegas Raiders. In Love's absence, the Cardinals have used a running back-by-committee approach with Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight. The backfield remained a near-even timeshare, with Knight continuing to show higher rushing efficiency while Allgeier matched him in receptions and receiving yards. Knight began to make a compelling case for a larger share of Arizona's backfield workload. Against the Rams in Week 6, he turned 15 carries into 80 yards, averaging an efficient 5.3 yards per attempt, while Allgeier managed just 38 yards on 18 carries. The trend continued in Week 7, as Knight generated 48 yards on only seven rushes compared to Allgeier's 19 yards on eight attempts, though Allgeier provided added value as a receiver with three catches for 30 yards. Arizona's rushing attack isn't overwhelming opponents with sheer talent. It's doing it with design, discipline, and deception. The Cardinals rank among the NFL's top 15 rushing offenses in both EPA per play and success rate, consistently using pulling linemen, multiple tight-end sets, and pre-snap motion to force defenders into hesitation and create favorable running lanes. The Cowboys' Cardinals problem isn't going away The Cardinals will play the Dallas Cowboys , an NFL franchise they've found a lot of success against recently, winning their last four matchups, and eight of the last nine, according to Ed Werder, Dallas Cowboys insider for WFAA. "The Cardinals (4) currently join Dallas' NFC East rivals Philadelphia (7), New York (5) and Washington (5) as the only teams with 4+ road wins at AT&T Stadium," Werder wrote on Oct. 27 . "Arizona's 4-game winning streak at AT&T Stadium is its longest winning streak at any road venue." Want more articles like this? Follow Yardbarker on MSN to see more of our exclusive NFL content. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
