picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . The Vikings are underdogs in this one for the second time this season. They were +4.5 underdogs in their 9-3 win in Chicago in Week 2. Detroit has now won two games in a row after falling in Carolina. The Lions blew out the Cardinals in Arizona heading into their bye and took care of business against the Packers last week. The Vikings won both meetings last season as +9.5 and +7.5 underdogs. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 8 matchup with a final score prediction. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is officially the most explosive division in football, and Ford Field will serve as ground zero this Sunday. The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense have regularly stalled, ranking 29th in total yards per game and managing just 20.7 points per game. To make matters more difficult, starting running back Aaron Jones Sr. is severely limited with a knee injury. The final bold prediction is that the Detroit Lions will win a high-scoring thriller, handing Minnesota its first loss of the 2026 season. The returning presence of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch gives Detroit's secondary the physical playmaking identity needed to keep Justin Jefferson under wraps. Ford Field will be deafening, and Detroit's offensive versatility will simply be too much to contain for all four quarters. Expect the Lions to walk away with a definitive statement win to tighten the race for the NFC North crown.

picks.headline: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8
picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. picks.headline: Raiders at Jets: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Jets vs Raiders odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Jets -1.5 Moneyline: Jets -125; Raiders +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Jets vs Raiders USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Jets 24, Raiders 21 Welcome back to Narrative Street! Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track. away.blurb: The Raiders’ defensive challenge starts before the throw. They need to communicate through motion, recognize changing formations and avoid leaving easy completions available when Stafford gets the ball out quickly. The Raiders should also be prepared for McVay to adjust around his available personnel. Los Angeles does not need every preferred receiving option healthy to build an effective passing plan. Washington was questionable with foot and back injuries. For Los Angeles, Puka Nacua was questionable with a calf injury, cornerback Trent McDuffie was questionable with a groin injury and linebacker Nate Landman was ruled out with a concussion. Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. away.headline: Steelers Could Get WR Back From Injury vs. Browns
away.blurb: Among the most notable storylines to come from the report is that wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) was ruled as questionable to play vs. Cleveland. He returned to practice as a limited participant this week, however, and now there's at least a chance that he'll suit up against the Browns. Given that the Steelers have been incredibly short-handed at receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list, however, Skowronek's potential return is a pretty big deal. As Skowronek is nearing a return, it appears as though Wilson and Pittman Jr. have good chances of returning down the line too. There was some concern that Pittman Jr. in particular would be out long-term, but head coach Mike McCarthy stated on October 29 that he thinks all of the Steelers' players on IR, "have a chance to come back," this season. Still, a potential Pittman Jr. return down the line would be massive news for a Steelers team that needs receiver help. home.headline: Steelers Could Get WR Back From Injury vs. Browns
home.blurb: Among the most notable storylines to come from the report is that wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) was ruled as questionable to play vs. Cleveland. He returned to practice as a limited participant this week, however, and now there's at least a chance that he'll suit up against the Browns. Given that the Steelers have been incredibly short-handed at receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list, however, Skowronek's potential return is a pretty big deal. As Skowronek is nearing a return, it appears as though Wilson and Pittman Jr. have good chances of returning down the line too. There was some concern that Pittman Jr. in particular would be out long-term, but head coach Mike McCarthy stated on October 29 that he thinks all of the Steelers' players on IR, "have a chance to come back," this season. Still, a potential Pittman Jr. return down the line would be massive news for a Steelers team that needs receiver help. home.headline: Todd Monken on the Steelers run game, Jared Verse, injuries, and more: Transcript
home.blurb: “Oh, for sure. I mean, there’s a number of reasons why they had the performance they did against us. Couple of misfits. Ball got out on us a couple of times, but we certainly can be a lot cleaner there with our fits, and Mike helps with that. In terms of disruption.” “Right, he played well. That remains to be seen. I mean, he’s been off a few weeks, but what I remember most is him coming back, from being knocked out and then coming back, wanting to be with his teammates and finishing the game. It says a lot that he came back to play. When you consider he’s been out since then, I think that says a lot more about him and how he’s wired.” “I just think in general, the personnel that you have dictates that a little bit. You’ve got to play the players that, the best 11. Not always, because situational football, you know, puts you in a – whether it’s short yardage, goal line, four-minute, where you’re trying to get bigger, or you’ve got to utilize different personnel groups at times. But certainly, you’d like to be multiple. Just like, from a personnel standpoint, you’d like to be multiple, just like from a schematic standpoint, you’d like to be multiple in terms of your run schemes, your pass schemes, that you’re good enough to win a game running it or throwing it, that makes it very hard to defend. You have enough skilled players where they’ve got to defend the field. They can’t cloud and tilt to one side. All that plays in together. And then how we scheme it. But you’d like to be as versatile as you can be, at least I would like to be. Now, if you’re fortunate enough to have players that can do it all, you don’t have to be as versatile. If you get, you know, tight ends that are three-down players and running backs are three-down players, and you get some of your wide outs that are not only elite route runners and can separate, but can go up and get it and be physical in the run game, the more tools they have, the less you have to, you know, rotate guys in and out to maximize their measurable skill set on game day. I kind of tried to say as much as I could in terms of that, but that’s kind of how you play into it a little bit.” I know you’ve said in the past that you like the fact that Jared Verse goes out and he backs up what he says. He’s kind of doubled down on some of his strong talk against the Steelers earlier, calling them dirty. He kind of doubled down on that yesterday. So just wondering, how are you feeling about some of the stuff that Jared is putting out there this week? “Oh, it’s never just one thing. Protection was better. We got the ball out better. We were able to run the ball better. We were ahead of the chains, we schemed guys open a little bit easier than we did the week before, where he was able to – he ended up holding it. Some was him; some was us. It’s never just one thing. I don’t think it was any different in terms of the way our players played, if that makes sense. The future first-ballot Hall of Famer is completing 61.6% of his passes. The Steelers improved to 5-2 by beating the New Orleans Saints in Paris in Week 7. Not only did the Steelers win their third straight game, but Rodgers also made incredible NFL history. Rodgers threw his 540th career touchdown pass, breaking a tie with NFL legend Peyton Manning on the career touchdown passes list. Rodgers now sits alone in third place with 540. Tom Brady threw 649 touchdowns with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He's in first place. Meanwhile, Drew Brees is in second place. He threw 571 with the San Diego Chargers and Saints. Pittsburgh is averaging 21.9 points per game in Year 1 of the McCarthy era. Rodgers and McCarthy led the Green Bay Packers to a Super Bowl XLV win against the Steelers back in 2011. They reunited this offseason. Rodgers has been a pro since 2005. The four-time MVP has played for the Packers, New York Jets and Steelers. Pittsburgh is tied with the Cleveland Browns at 5-2 in the AFC North. However, the Browns beat the Steelers a couple of weeks ago, so technically, Cleveland is in first place in the division. The Steelers host the Browns next week, so Rodgers and Co. must win that game to avoid going 0-2 against Cleveland this season. Rodgers had 3,322 passing yards, 24 passing touchdowns and seven interceptions last season. The Steelers won the AFC North but lost to the Houston Texans in the wild-card round of the playoffs. Can Rodgers win a Super Bowl in his final NFL season like Manning did with the Denver Broncos? Only time will tell. The odds are pretty low since the Steelers have many flaws on both sides of the ball. However, we said the same thing about the 2010 Packers, and they shocked the world by winning the Super Bowl. It's their last division matchup before closing the year with three straight NFC South games. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the 66th time on Sunday, reigniting a series that has been exceptionally close. Atlanta leads the head-to-head 33-32, and each of the last six games between the two teams has been decided by six points or fewer. That includes the Falcons' 29-28 victory last season in Week 15, which featured a 15-point, fourth-quarter rally by Atlanta and a career game from tight end Kyle Pitts. Both teams head into this game off rejuvenating wins. A potent rushing attack that generated 258 yards on the ground and a defense that created four turnovers propelled the Buccaneers to a 43-13 win against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons also forced four turnovers and got a strong performance from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to earn a 29-20 win and hand the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season. After the Panthers lost to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night, the Falcons would gain sole possession of first place in the NFC South with a victory on Sunday. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and Buccaneers. picks.blurb: Falcons vs. Buccaneers Expert Pick | NFL Week 8 2026 Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE KREWE MEMBERS The national analysts are leaning towards the Falcons in Sunday's NFC South showdown at Raymond James Stadium, but some expect a motivated Baker Mayfield to swing the balance Scott Smith Senior Writer/Editor The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come back home in Week Eight trying to turn a rousing road victory at Carolina into a streak within NFC South divisional play, as the Atlanta Falcons visit on Sunday. The Falcons are also riding high, having dispatched a previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers team last Sunday, and they bring serious firepower to Raymond James Stadium in the quartet of Michael Penix, Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts. To find out how to watch, listen and livestream the game, click here . Several analysts noted that both teams want to run the ball but will be facing defenses that are hard to run against. One analyst called the two squads "mirror images" in their strengths and weaknesses. One reporter suggested this was a Baker Mayfield game – that his performance would swing the balance – and that he might have some extra motivation going against a Kevin Stefanski-led team. Another pointed out that both teams have struggled to make winning plays at the very end of one-score games, and yet another thought the possible return of Emeka Egbuka for the Bucs would be significant. Perhaps the expert who put it best was the one who called it a "box of chocolates" game with these two teams: You never know what you're going to get. Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford sided with the Falcons in a tight matchup and explains why: "Both the Falcons and Buccaneers have stellar run defenses, so this game may come down to which QB plays better. The Bucs beat the Panthers in Baker Mayfield's return to the field, but that was more about leaning on the run game than Mayfield steering the ship. Michael Penix Jr. has six touchdowns in his last two starts, including three in the Falcons' Week 7 upset win over the 49ers. I think Atlanta will carry that momentum and earn a big NFC South win here." The Buccaneers are 1.5-point favorites at home but the majority of analysts seem to disagree with that assessment. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Despite each team being below .500, Sunday’s NFC South matchup at Raymond James Stadium between the Falcons (3-4) and the Buccaneers (2-5) is a battle for first place. Yes, with Carolina losing Thursday night to Green Bay, no team in the NFC South is even .500. Atlanta sits tied with Carolina entering the weekend, while Tampa Bay sits just one game back despite losing its first four games. Atlanta snapped a two-game losing streak last Sunday with arguably its best win of the season, knocking off the previously unbeaten 49ers, 29-20. Michael Penix Jr. completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, throwing scoring passes to Nick Muse , Kyle Pitts Sr . and Drake London , while Atlanta’s defense produced four takeaways and scored 13 points off San Francisco turnovers. Penix has helped stabilize the Falcons after their 0-2 start, and Sunday represents a homecoming for the Tampa-area native. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, dismantled Carolina 43-13 last week in Baker Mayfield’s return after missing three games with a dislocated thumb. The Bucs own the league’s third-ranked rushing attack and they played to their strength against the Panthers attempting only 11 passes while piling up 258 rushing yards on 49 carries. Bucky Irving ran for a chunk of the 258 yards totaling 106 yards and two touchdowns. Tampa’s defense added four takeaways and five sacks. The Falcons’ defensive front and playmaking secondary were difference-makers against San Francisco, but Tampa Bay has topped 240 rushing yards in two of its last three victories and with Emeka Egbuka declared OUT of Sunday’s game, the Bucs will look to their run game to be the difference-maker against a Falcons’ team that will undoubtedly stack the box. Atlanta leads the all-time series 33-32, and the Falcons won both meetings last season. Their most recent matchup, also at Raymond James Stadium on Dec. 11, 2025, produced one of the rivalry’s wildest finishes. Tampa Bay led 28-14 in the fourth quarter, but Kirk Cousins rallied Atlanta with two late touchdown drives, including his third TD pass of the night to Kyle Pitts , before Zane Gonzalez hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired for a 29-28 Falcons victory. away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions in the Jaguars' showdown with the Colts, starting with Josh Hines-Allen
picks.blurb: Josh Hines-Allen and the Jacksonville Jaguars have heard about the pass rush all bye week. Jacksonville is paying Hines-Allen, Travon Walker and Arik Armstead a combined $63 million this season, and the three have 4.5 sacks through six games. The Indianapolis Colts come to EverBank Stadium on Sunday with a quarterback who goes down a lot. Indianapolis (2-5) has lost three straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard and then traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. Jacksonville (4-2) comes off a 34-31 loss to Houston in London and has won the last two meetings in the series. “This has to all be about our improvements, us getting back on track,” head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday, per the team’s website . The Jaguars are a big home favorite . Here are four bold predictions for the first game out of the bye. Josh Hines-Allen leads a four-sack day Daniel Jones has been sacked 19 times, per NFL.com , including six times against Tennessee and four more in Minnesota. Now he’s without Nelson, and rookie fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer is expected to take over at left guard . Hines-Allen has 17 pressures and a 77.1 grade that ranks 18th among 113 edge defenders, according to PFF . Walker leads the team with two sacks. We laid out the pass-rush fix the Jaguars need during the bye, and this is the matchup to make it. Bold prediction: Jacksonville sacks Jones four times, and Hines-Allen gets at least one. Parker Washington goes over 100 yards Parker Washington has 26 catches for 416 yards and four touchdowns, and his 81.6 grade ranks 13th among 76 receivers, according to PFF . He went for 124 yards and two scores against Philadelphia in London, and he has become Trevor Lawrence’s top target . Indianapolis is thin at corner. Sauce Gardner has a 62.6 coverage grade, 47th among corners, per PFF , and was limited Wednesday with a calf injury before practicing fully Thursday. Justin Walley missed both days with a knee injury, and the Colts put Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve this week. Bold prediction: Washington tops 100 yards and catches his fifth touchdown. Travis Hunter intercepts Daniel Jones Travis Hunter caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud in the end zone in London, per the Jaguars . He has two interceptions on 311 snaps at corner, and his 69.0 coverage grade ranks 23rd among 101 corners, according to PFF . Jones has seven interceptions, and his 48.3 passing grade ranks 32nd of 35 quarterbacks, according to PFF . Jacksonville’s pass defense still has communication issues to clean up , and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile put it simply. “No defense can overcome giving up chunk plays,” he said, per the team’s website . Bold prediction: Hunter gets his third interception. Brian Thomas Jr. catches a touchdown Brian Thomas Jr. has nine catches for 105 yards, and he was benched at halftime in London after a career-low 15 snaps. “I really just wanted to flush it, come back ready with a different mindset, come back ready to go,” he said this week, per The Associated Press . His name sits at the top of the Jaguars’ trade rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, but Coen expects him to help. “He’s going to be able to help us make plays this week. I bet it. I know it,” Coen said, per The Associated Press . Bold prediction: Thomas catches his second touchdown of the season, and Duval gets a reminder of why the Jaguars drafted him in the first round. Erickson Nathan Brown Indianapolis Star Oct. 30, 2026, 6:13 a.m. ET All the action with the Indianapolis Colts this week has been in the front office, but there's a game to play Sunday, Nov. 1. The Colts (2-5) visit Jacksonville to play the AFC South-leading Jaguars (4-2) at 1 p.m. ET, and Indianapolis has several things working against it: All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive leader DeForest Buckner have been traded away. For the second straight week, the Colts visit an opponent coming off a bye week. The Colts haven't won in Jacksonville for more than a decade. Do the Colts have a chance? Here's what the expert predictions say: Are the Colts favored against the Jaguars ? away.headline: Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report
away.blurb: In return for the All-Pro guard, the Colts received a 2027 third round pick and 2028 fifth round pick from Seattle. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLTS Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report Cameron Cocquyt Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 1:39 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Nelson had reportedly wanted to sign a long-term contract extension to remain with the Colts. In exchange for Nelson, Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. After the Indianapolis Colts fired general manger Chris Ballard 10 days ago, it sent a ripple effect down the organization. Coming off a second-half letdown and loss to the then 0-5 Tennessee Titans , it seemed clear that changes were imminent. Tuesday, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks , a franchise cornerstone on the offensive line since Indianapolis drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . With uncertainty surrounding the future of the organization, rumors began to swirl about trade requests regarding some of the Colts' most important players. ESPN NFL insider Ian Rapoport joined the Pat McAfee show Wednesday and shed some light on Nelson's situation in Indianapolis. "Is that accurate? He wanted to get a deal done with Indianapolis this off-season," McAfee asked Rapoport. "Yeah, that is true." Rapoport replied. "When Chris Ballard was there, I really thought it was going to get done." Nelson didn't sign an extension. He is currently on the final year of a four-year, $80 million contract, his first large-scale extension following his rookie contract. According to Rapoport, it was up to Nelson if he would be spending the next several years with the Colts' organization. "This is a huge bounty for someone in the middle of the season," Rapoport added. "A lot of people wanted this guy that the Seahawks think is like really, really going to help their run game." Since arriving in Indianapolis, Nelson was selected to the Pro Bowl each of his eight seasons and was named an All-Pro in six of those. Just a short time after Nelson's trade, the Colts moved another key piece of the roster in DeForest Buckner , who returns to the organization that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers . Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick. With uncertainty surrounding the organization, there is reason to believe the roster moves won't stop here. away.headline: Colts' injury report includes good news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner, bad news on Justin Walley
away.blurb: Indianapolis will be without starting slot corner Justin Walley , who suffered a knee injury late in Sunday’s road loss to the Vikings and did not practice this week, as well as the team’s first corner off the bench, veteran Cam Taylor-Britt , who landed on injured reserve this week with a groin injury also suffered late in Sunday’s 16-10 loss. The Colts will also get back starting tight end Tyler Warren , who missed the team’s last two games with a groin injury. Warren logged his first practice of any kind Thursday after suffering the injury Oct. 23 before a Week 6 game against the Titans where he didn’t appear as a game-time decision. Warren, the team’s leader in catches (30), missed all of last week’s practice, too, as well as the Week 7 game. He was limited in Thursday’s practice but then participated fully Friday. Along with Walley, the Colts also ruled out wide receiver Anthony Gould for Sunday’s game as the return specialist continues to work his way back from a concussion suffered in Week 6. Gould returned to practice this week and was full both days but needs to clear the league’s concussion protocol. Tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) and Bryce Boettcher (groin) are listed as questionable for Sunday’s game. Ogletree was limited in Thursday’s practice and then did not participate Friday, and Boettcher missed both outings after practicing once last week but missing Sunday’s Week 7 game. With Boettcher’s role Sunday in question, all signs point to rookie linebacker C.J. Allen making his first start of his NFL career, as he returns from an ankle injury he suffered last week in practice that sidelined him Sunday. Allen was a full participant in both the Colts’ practices this week. INDIANAPOLIS – The Colts have gotten mixed injury updates at cornerback this week heading into a road divisional game Sunday in Jacksonville as heavy underdogs. Down two of its top four corners, though, the Colts will get starting outside corner Sauce Gardner back after the All-Pro left midway through the team’s Week 6 game with an injury to his left calf. Gardner then didn’t practice all last week and missed Sunday’s game. He was a full participant in the Colts’ two practices this week. Start the day smarter. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. BFTB community, how do you feel about the Chargers possibly getting their first win of the season against the Rams at SoFi Stadium in Week 8? Let us know in the comments section below.

picks.blurb: Chargers-Rams Game Preview: How does Joe Alt’s return improve the Bolts’ offense? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Joe Alt (76) stands by during a timeout during an NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA.(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Michael Peterson Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:28 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Bolts are back inside SoFi Stadium this week to face the crosstown Rams. The Rams are also failing to meet expectations this season with a 3-4 record so far this season. Blockbuster addition Myles Garrett has not played since Week One, but that's far from their only issue. When it's all firing, Sean McVay and the Rams are still one of the best teams in the league, so the Chargers need to come as correct a ever (and unfortunately, the next time they do will be the first). Expectations are likely low, but they don't say "any given Sunday" for no reason. Here are the three things I'll be watching for when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) Can the Chargers secondary take advantage of a Rams WR unit missing Davante Adams? The Chargers are dodging longtime and All-Pro wideout Davate Adams this week after he recently landed on IR. The Rams offense is now a bit more palatable, but Puka Nacua is still the real deal as one of the most productive wideouts in the league over the past few seasons. The Chargers cornerback room has held strong with Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart staying healthy this season. Veteran Donte Jackson has been more out of the lineup than in and the same can be said for both Rodney Shelley and Deane Leonard. Cornerback could be a big need this offseason, but that's a whole other conversation. With the Rams using a ton of motion pre-snap, I expect the Chargers to play a lot of zone to keep Still or Hart from having to travel across the formation. The lack of Derwin James continues to hurt, but overall they've been fine enough without him. This will be an interesting test for Chris O'Leary. Aside from the continuous short fields given by the offense, the young coordinator has done an admirable job against some of the league's top offensive play-callers. Showing he has the stuff to take on McVay could be another early feather in his cap. 2.) Will Joe Alt switch to left tackle in his return from a neck injury? Last season when Rashawn Slater missed the entire season due to a torn patellar tendon, Alt flipped sides from right to left. This year, Alt is about to return to the lineup without Slater once more. I'm curious to see if they believe rookie Travis, who has played the past few games at left tackle, can continue to do so which would allow Alt to remain at his normal spot. Alt has been one of the best tackles in all of football. His return is huge. Knowing how bad the offense has been, I would not be surprised to see Burke go to the right side to allow Alt to protect Justin Herbert's blindside. That seems like the most important thing to cover as far as getting this front five pinned down. Kayode Awosika was expected to return after the bye, but he remains a non-participant in practice. That leaves rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Not especially ideal given how rough he's been as a starter, but that's what happens when there's three players at his position hurt ahead of him. So for Week Eight, Alt is the only returning player who wasn't healthy before the bye. And again, his return is a big deal, but is it as big as it sounds? The offense wasn't good when the majority of the team is healthy. How much will it really change for the offense as a whole? 3.) Will the offense look any different post-bye? This one is as simple as it sounds. The Chargers chose not to make any massive changes at the bye despite sitting at 0-6. Mike McDaniel not only still has his job, but he will remain the offensive playcaller going forward. Even if you did not expect McDaniel to get fired last week, you likely also thought there'd at least be some change on the coaching staff. So here the Chargers are, in the same boat that they rode to the league's worst offense. Harbaugh has decided that six weeks wasn't enough to make a decision and with no trades having been made, they whole franchise supposedly believes it's worth keeping all their assets in order to make an effort towards the unprecedented. No team has ever made the playoffs after starting 0-5. The Chargers are 0-6. I seriously do not know what the plan is. Will 0-7 force a change? 0-8? Where is the line in the sand? If Justin Herbert avoids throwing an interception in a game for the first time all season, will that be all the team needs to believe they've fixed it? Does he need to do it for consecutive games? It sure feels like the bar is set way to low for things to keep chugging along like they haven't already been off the tracks since Week One.

away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday’s game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn’t participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington’s back locked up in practice, which is why he’ll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers’ side, they’ll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. home.blurb: Head coach Sean McVay stated the reason for the addition was due to current long snapper Joe Cardona picking up an ankle injury. If McQuaide does play, he will be the sixth specialist to take a snap for Los Angeles this season, joining Cardona, Ethan Evans, Harrison Mevis, Blake Grupe, and Brandon McManus. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams’ special teams unit gets more bad news with long snapper doubtful The Los Angeles Rams made the surprising decision this week to sign veteran long snapper Jake McQuaide to their practice squad. McQuaide and the Rams have a great relationship, and McQuaide joins Aaron Donald as the only two active players with franchise who played during their time in St. Louis. McQuaide was the Rams' long-snapper to end the 2025 season, replacing Alex Ward. He was excellent, helping the team reach the NFC Championship Game. He also played for the Rams from 2011 to 2020, earning Pro Bowl honors in 2016 and 2017. McQuaide also played for the Dallas Cowboys, Detroit Lions , Chicago Bears , Minnesota Vikings , Miami Dolphins , and Pittsburgh Steelers, either as a member of the active roster or the practice squad.

home.blurb: Offensive guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) were once again non-participants. There was hope both could return this week, but they're slated to miss yet another week at this rate. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. picks.blurb: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chiefs Rematch Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 with a few prime objectives, the first of which is winning the AFC West. The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21 Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16 James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14 Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown. Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24 Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season.
