picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

picks.headline: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
picks.blurb: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jared Sapp Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Denver Broncos — in their second meeting of the year — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 5-2 Broncos have rebounded since being dominated by the Chiefs to open the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 1.5-point road favorites. Denver's quarterback play under Bo Nix has been a hotly debated topic in 2026, and their defense has not always lived up to the standard set in recent years. But the Broncos are coming off of their best overall performance of the year — a 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) One of the Chiefs' biggest priorities should be finding a way to lessen Kenneth Walker's workload. This is not the week for that. Denver is playing better, but the middle of the defense can still be attacked and will be the Chiefs' best path to win. This is a week where we can overreact to Week 7 and how inept the Chiefs looked against the league's best defense while Denver was comfortably beating the Arizona Cardinals. The strengths and weaknesses both teams have shown through the first half of the season are still there. I expect a much closer result than Week 1, but I think the Chiefs can still play smart football and ride a run heavy approach to a close victory. Chiefs 20, Broncos 16 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) This matchup will be critical for the outcome of the AFC West, as well as for playoff seeding. Bo Nix is coming off of maybe his best offensive performance of the season while Mahomes is coming off of his worse. That said, Nix has still struggled to create consistency this year, and the Chiefs defense has already gotten the better of him once. I expect the Chiefs to come out with a better offensive plan — but the line must be able to protect for Patrick Mahomes. In the end, it will be interesting to see how much the Chiefs use of Kenneth Walker and the play action passing game affects the Denver defense this week. Chiefs 24, Broncos 17 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) The Chiefs dominated the Broncos in Week 1, and while I expect Denver to put up a better fight at home, I still don't trust their ability to stop the run. Kenneth Walker should bounce back after a disappointing performance in Seattle, and if Rashee Rice returns, Patrick Mahomes gets one of his favorite weapons back. On the other side, I just don't trust Bo Nix and that Broncos offense to consistently sustain drives against Kansas City. Give me the Chiefs to take care of business and put a stranglehold on the AFC West. Chiefs 20, Broncos 17 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) This is a chance for the Chiefs to take a firm grip on the AFC West. A win over Denver would give Kansas City a season sweep and valuable separation from its biggest division challenger. But I don't expect another convincing win like the season opener. Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense have found more rhythm, and while I'm not sold on him as a dominant quarterback, he has shown he can make timely plays. Patrick Surtain's potential return would strengthen Denver's defense, although Jaylon Waddle's uncertain availability could leave its receiving corps shorthanded. The Chiefs got punched in the face in Seattle, but I trust their veteran leadership and coaching staff to respond. That starts with getting Kenneth Walker III going and giving Patrick Mahomes better protection. Jaylon Moore's potential return and the possibility of getting Rice back would help, while I'd like to see more downfield opportunities for the younger receivers. Defensively, I'm looking for more Chris Roland-Wallace in the slot and fewer snaps there for L'Jarius Sneed. Ultimately, I expect Walker to lead the way, Mahomes to bounce back and Kansas City to regain control after its first loss. Chiefs 27, Broncos 17 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) What has really changed since the Chiefs beat the Broncos 31-10 in Week one? The Chiefs followed that win with 4 others vs AFC opponents. They ran into a buzz saw in Seattle for sure — once again exposing the limits of the Chiefs OL and WR depth. Some help seems to be on the way, whether that impacts this weekend's game or not, we'll see. Butthis IS still the same Chiefs team from the first 5 weeks. They'll be able to run the ball again and Mahomes will bounce back with a vengeance. They may not put up 30 points against a good Denver defense, but I'd bet on competence. Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) A lot is on the line in this one. I don't see the Chiefs laying an egg like they did last week. But they won't dominate Denver like they did Week 1 either. Rashee Rice's likely return will help the offense. I also don't see the Broncos completely shutting down Walker and the Chiefs' running game. The defense will play better, although I think our pass rush will remain a major issue against the Broncos' offensive line. This one will be a close divisional battle, and I think it comes down to the wire. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) As good as Denver's defense is, their secondary is not as good as the Seattle Seahawks'. Neither is their run defense. And the biggest fact of all, they don't have the best wide receiver in the universe as Seattle does. I expect Kenneth Walker to continue to be the best running back in the NFL, and I expect the Chiefs to make Bo Nix look as bad or worse than he has all season. Last week wasn't a sign that the NFL has figured out the Chiefs. It was never hard to figure out Kansas City's offense. Stop the run and the Chiefs are in trouble. But that's easier said than done. And I don't think Denver can do it. Chiefs 19, Broncos 10 Nate Christensen This game has massive stakes for divisional seeding purposes, but also for the direction of both teams the rest of the year. Denver is trying to prove that Week 1 was a fluke and that their offense is good enough to beat the best teams in the NFL. Kansas City is trying to prove that they can move the ball against a very stingy Broncos defense again, particularly one that will be much more keyed on stopping Kenneth Walker. Unfortunately for the Chiefs, I worry about that. The Chiefs passing offense has looked bad against both Denver and Seattle, which feature top-5 passing defenses. I expect that to continue, and I think Denver does a better job stopping the run to close this game out. I expect the Chiefs defense to keep this close and potentially carry them to a win, but I think Denver splits the series at home. Broncos 17, Chiefs 13 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) The Seattle loss felt like it was coming from miles away, and this always felt like the real measuring-stick game for the Chiefs through the first half of the season. In Denver, where they lost 22-19 last year and essentially handed the division over to the Broncos. This Sunday, Kansas City can take the reins of the AFC West back, and I see them rising to the occasion. The Broncos' run defense is the weakness of a strong unit, and I see running back Kenneth Walker bouncing back in a huge way against the team he ran for more than 170 rushing yards against in Week 1. The offense gets back on track this week, especially with right tackle Jaylon Moore back in the lineup. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

Kansas City Chiefs star rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane popped up on the team's injury report on Thursday as a non-participant with a shoulder injury. However, the team isn't giving up hope that he could still play in its Week 8 matchup against the Denver Broncos. It is certainly good news, given the nature of the injury. Delane dealt with a shoulder injury in training camp and then reaggravated it in Week 1. So, it could be that the injury is flaring up once again. However, the Chiefs' decision to keep the door open for him to play in Week 8 signifies that it doesn't look to be too serious. Delane has quickly established himself as one of the best up-and-coming defenders in the league, recording 27 tackles, five passes defensed and one interception through five games. away.headline: Broncos rule RJ Harvey, Talanoa Hufanga out against Chiefs, slew of key players questionable
away.blurb: Jaylen Waddle, Zach Allen, Garett Bolles and Brandon Jones are all questionable to play vs. Kansas City The Broncos will be without a pair of key contributors Sunday against Kansas City and a quartet of foundational players are listed as questionable. Running back RJ Harvey will miss the game after sustaining a knee injury in Thursday's practice, while safety Talanoa Hufanga is out for a third straight game with an ankle injury. Denver is also listing defensive tackle Zach Allen (hamstring), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), left tackle Garett Bolles (hip), and safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) as questionable. All four were limited participants in practice Friday. Harvey injury is not believed to be severe or hold him out long term, a source told The Post. He's already been ruled out for the Chiefs' game, but it's an encouraging sign for the Broncos' running back. It is not immediately clear how much time he will miss or if he is a candidate for injured reserve. Denver typically places players on IR on Saturday before a game. With Harvey out Sunday and fellow running back Tyler Badie already on injured reserve with a thumb issue, the Broncos will rely heavily on rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. They are also likely to promote Cody Schrader from the practice squad and have at times used fullback Adam Prentice as a pass protector this year. “I’m ready for any opportunity I’m given,” he said. “Whenever I'm out there, I’m going to give the team my all.” Hufanga, meanwhile, was present at Denver’s practice Friday for the first time since he hurt his ankle Oct. 11 at the Los Angeles Chargers. He was listed as a non-participant, however. With Hufanga out and Jones questionable, the Broncos will elevate veteran Taylor Rapp for the third and final time from the practice squad unless he is promoted to the 53-man roster before Sunday. He has filled in ably the past two weeks with Hufanga down. Waddle and Allen were injured in the fourth quarter of last week’s win at Arizona while Jones dropped out of Thursday’s practice with the hamstring issue. The fact that they and Bolles both practiced in a limited capacity over the past two days is a promising sign, though there is enough uncertainty about their game statuses to list them as questionable. Jones practicing one day after dropping out with a hamstring issue is also a positive sign. Kansas City's list of players up in the air for Sunday isn't as long as Denver's, but several key defenders are either out or questionable. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed was ruled out by the team Friday with a knee injury while a pair of standout rookies in cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and edge rusher R Mason Thomas (personal) are questionable to play. Delane practiced Wednesday but then was a DNP each of the past two days with a shoulder injury. He picked off Bo Nix on the first possession of Week 1 but then didn't return due to a shoulder injury. away.headline: Denver Broncos Get Bad RJ Harvey News Before Chiefs Game
away.blurb: Denver ruled RJ Harvey out for Sunday's game with a knee injury, confirming his absence after he missed practice Friday. The second-year back had appeared on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant. Broncos Rule RJ Harvey Out With Knee Injury He was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, was limited Thursday with a knee issue and did not participate Friday. Denver then ruled him out for the Chiefs game. Denver Broncos Get Bad RJ Harvey News Before Chiefs Game Unlock the latest Heavy on Broncos news — direct to your inbox. The Denver Broncos will face the Kansas City Chiefs without a running back who delivered one of their biggest plays last week. What began as a new injury concern Thursday is now a confirmed loss for an offense preparing for an AFC West matchup. Harvey scored on a 52-yard reception in Denver's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals on October 25. Earlier Friday, DNVR Sports reporter Zac Stevens reported that coach Sean Payton did not comment on Harvey's status. The Broncos' final injury report subsequently supplied the answer: Harvey will not play. Harvey's practice participation changed quickly during the week. The designation settles his availability for Sunday. It does not establish a longer recovery timeline or provide a specific diagnosis beyond the knee injury listed by the team. Harvey's absence removes a receiving option for quarterback Bo Nix , even as Denver has divided rushing opportunities among multiple backs. According to his official team statistics , Harvey has caught 25 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown through six appearances this season. He has added 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 24 carries. His performance against Arizona illustrated the difference between those contributions. Harvey gained six yards on three carries but caught two passes for 54 yards, including the 52-yard touchdown on a screen pass. Replacing him requires more than redistributing a handful of rushing attempts. Denver also loses a back who turned a short throw into a touchdown in its most recent game. J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman Face Bigger Opportunity Payton discussed Denver's backfield Friday without detailing Harvey's condition. According to Stevens, Payton said the Broncos use a hot-hand approach at times. Stevens also reported that Payton pointed to analytics when discussing J.K. Dobbins' burst and speed and described the running back room as deep. That depth now faces another test, with Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman positioned to absorb additional work. Coleman returned against Arizona after missing four games with an ankle injury. He rushed nine times for 54 yards and added two catches for 15 yards, giving Denver 69 scrimmage yards in his first game back. Payton had already called for more opportunities for the rookie before Harvey's knee issue appeared on the injury report. "He looked really good. Got to get him more touches," Payton said after the Arizona game, according to the Broncos' official coverage .

away.headline: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL NFL injury tracker live updates Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty Images Harrison Butker has made plenty of big-time kicks for the Chiefs over the past decade, but he seems to be on the decline. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

Waddle is their No. 1 receiver, having acquired him in a trade with the Miami Dolphins during this past offseason. The injuries don't stop with Waddle for Denver. It has officially ruled out key players such as safety Talanoa Hufanga and running back RJ Harvey. Hufanga is one of the best safeties in the league, and Harvey is a dual threat as a runner and receiver. If Waddle is out in addition to Hufanga and Harvey, it could be tough sledding for the Broncos. Denver has also listed offensive tackle Garett Bolles, safety Brandon Jones, and defensive lineman Zach Allen as questionable. All three players are starters. home.blurb: Denver ruled RJ Harvey out for Sunday's game with a knee injury, confirming his absence after he missed practice Friday. The second-year back had appeared on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant. Broncos Rule RJ Harvey Out With Knee Injury He was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, was limited Thursday with a knee issue and did not participate Friday. Denver then ruled him out for the Chiefs game. Denver Broncos Get Bad RJ Harvey News Before Chiefs Game Unlock the latest Heavy on Broncos news — direct to your inbox. The Denver Broncos will face the Kansas City Chiefs without a running back who delivered one of their biggest plays last week. What began as a new injury concern Thursday is now a confirmed loss for an offense preparing for an AFC West matchup. Harvey scored on a 52-yard reception in Denver's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals on October 25. Earlier Friday, DNVR Sports reporter Zac Stevens reported that coach Sean Payton did not comment on Harvey's status. The Broncos' final injury report subsequently supplied the answer: Harvey will not play. Harvey's practice participation changed quickly during the week. The designation settles his availability for Sunday. It does not establish a longer recovery timeline or provide a specific diagnosis beyond the knee injury listed by the team. Harvey's absence removes a receiving option for quarterback Bo Nix , even as Denver has divided rushing opportunities among multiple backs. According to his official team statistics , Harvey has caught 25 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown through six appearances this season. He has added 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 24 carries. His performance against Arizona illustrated the difference between those contributions. Harvey gained six yards on three carries but caught two passes for 54 yards, including the 52-yard touchdown on a screen pass. Replacing him requires more than redistributing a handful of rushing attempts. Denver also loses a back who turned a short throw into a touchdown in its most recent game. J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman Face Bigger Opportunity Payton discussed Denver's backfield Friday without detailing Harvey's condition. According to Stevens, Payton said the Broncos use a hot-hand approach at times. Stevens also reported that Payton pointed to analytics when discussing J.K. Dobbins' burst and speed and described the running back room as deep. That depth now faces another test, with Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman positioned to absorb additional work. Coleman returned against Arizona after missing four games with an ankle injury. He rushed nine times for 54 yards and added two catches for 15 yards, giving Denver 69 scrimmage yards in his first game back. Payton had already called for more opportunities for the rookie before Harvey's knee issue appeared on the injury report. "He looked really good. Got to get him more touches," Payton said after the Arizona game, according to the Broncos' official coverage .

picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. The Dolphins will play at Gillette Stadium in the second game to close out the 2026 regular season. The date and time for that game have not been announced yet. Last season, the Patriots swept the series with a 33-27 win at Miami (9/14) and a 38-10 win to close out the 2025 regular season at Gillette Stadium (1/4). The Patriots will look to win their third straight game over the Dolphins and go 3-0 in the AFC East. The Patriots and Dolphins will meet for the second time in 2026 in the regular season finale at Gillette Stadium in a game that is not scheduled at this time. It will be the 19th time that the two teams will square off in the final game of the year and the second straight year that the Patriots will host the game. Nine of those final games have been played in New England with the Patriots holding a 5-4 edge in those games. Overall, the Patriots are 9-8 when facing Miami in the final game of the year. New England has the advantage against Miami in home games, leading the series 39-21 - including 18-6 at Gillette Stadium - but are 18-43 when playing on the road against Miami. The Dolphins and Patriots met for the first time in 1966 and began playing twice a year during the 1967 regular season, except in 1982 during a players' strike. The two teams have played three times in the postseason with New England holding a 2-1 advantage. Photo by Eric J. He needs 2 rushing touchdowns to tie Curtis Martin and Tony Collins for sixth place on the Patriots alltime list for rushing touchdowns. He has had 2 rushing touchdowns in a game six times, with the last coming in the 2025 season-finale vs. Miami on Jan. 4, 2026. Stevenson has 206 career receptions and joined Kevin Faulk (431), James White (381), Tony Collins (261) and Sam Cunningham (210) as the only New England running backs with 200 receptions. He needs 4 receptions to tie Sam Cunningham for fourth place among all Patriots running backs in career receptions. Stevenson (3,954) needs 46 yards to join Sam Cunningham (5,453), Jim Nance (5,323) and Tony Collins (4,647) as the only Patriots players to reach 4,000 rushing yards. Stevenson had a career-high 93 yards receiving last week at Chicago. If he registers at least 90 yards receiving this week, he will become just the second Patriots running back with back-to-back games with at least 90 yards receiving. RB Ron Burton had 94 yards receiving at Houston on Nov. 18, 1962 and followed that performance with 97 yards receiving on Nov. 23, 1962 vs. Buffalo. Stevenson enters this week in 22nd place on the Patriots all-time scoring list with 220 points. Weight: 225 lbs College: North Carolina QB Drake Maye completed a 48-yard touchdown pass to RB Rhamondre Stevenson at the end of the second quarter last week at Chicago for his 11th touchdown of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. He then threw a 30-yard touchdown pass to TE Eli Raridon in the third quarter for his 12th, the most in the NFL over that span. Josh Allen and Jalen Hurts each have nine touchdowns of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. It is Maye's second 40-yard touchdown pass of the 2026 season. The Patriots record for most consecutive games in a season with at least 2 touchdown passes is 10 by Tom Brady in 2007 and 2014. Maye threw for 321 yards last week against Chicago. If he throws for 300 yards this week against Miami, he will be the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300-yard games since Tom Brady in 2019 when he threw for 348 yards at Washington (10/6) and 334 yards vs. the New York Giants (10/10). Bernd Buchmasser, Matt St. Jean, Pat Lane and Dylan Klayman contributed to this story. After enjoying a weekend off, the New England Patriots are back in action this Sunday. Their opponent coming out of the mini-bye is a familiar one, at least on paper: the Miami Dolphins. However, these are not the same Dolphins that lost both of their games to the Patriots in 2025. Led by new head coach Jeff Hafley, they have overhauled significant portions of their roster and staff. Are they better off as a result? So far, the record doesn’t say so. That said, unlike the Patriots, the Dolphins are entering Week 8 off a victory — their first of the season. Still, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Patriots are seen as seven-point favorites entering the game. Will they live up to that status? Or will the Dolphins manage to defend their home turf? Let’s find out what Pats Pulpit’s staff and community think. away.headline: AJ Brown injury update, latest news on Patriots WR's status for game vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after missing practice this week with a knee injury. Brown was listed as limited with ankle and knee injuries on the Patriots' Wednesday injury report and did not practice in Thursday's session. When asked Wednesday if he was still working on regaining his explosiveness after his return from IR, Brown said, "Sometimes I see it, and sometimes I'm pushing through." NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the news on Thursday, noting the issue "flared up" and that his status for Sunday is "up in the air." Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf told Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein after acquiring Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June the wide receiver had a " degenerative knee condition ." "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Epstein in June. "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots are already missing Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins after the wide receivers were placed on injured reserve with shoulder and calf injuries, respectively. Pop Douglas was serving as the Patriots' WR1 in front of Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III with Brown absent from Thursday's practice, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown's potential absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games. Stevenson, who also ranks fifth on the Patriots in receiving yards, could step up in the long term. Brown's absence still raises concerns about his long-term future before the three-year, $96 million extension he signed with the Eagles in 2024 kicks in next season.

away.blurb: While speaking with reporters on Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Brown "is questionable" for this coming Sunday's game between 4-3 New England and the 1-5 Miami Dolphins at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium. Could A.J. Brown be a game-time decision for Dolphins game? As Rodney Knuppel of NESN pointed out, the Patriots were already set to be without receivers Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins before Brown missed multiple practices this week. Thus, fourth-year pro DeMario Douglas could end up being the favorite target of quarterback Drake Maye against the Dolphins. Christian Watson details gritty return to Packers' 'TNF' win over Panthers after breaking rib, spitting up blood A familiar issue popped up on the New England Patriots ' injury report when it was learned earlier in the week that wide receiver A.J. Brown wasn't practicing due to a knee injury. "We'll see how he comes in tomorrow, and then we'll make a decision," Vrabel said about Brown, per Greg A. Bedard of Boston Sports Journal. Brown's history of dealing with what has been referred to as a " degenerative knee condition " is well-known among members of the NFL community. It was reported this past spring that the Los Angeles Rams passed on attempting to acquire Brown because they allegedly didn't want to match the Philadelphia Eagles ' asking price for his services due to concerns related to his knee. More recently, Brown suggested he still wasn't 100 percent in his ongoing recovery from the high ankle sprain he suffered in the Patriots' 13-10 season-opening loss at the Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 9. Brown returned to the lineup on Oct. 18, and he tallied six catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns on 16 targets over his first two games back. Bedard noted that Vrabel was asked on Friday whether the Patriots may have rushed Brown back from the ankle injury. "I don't think those things are really ... I think those are separate issues here," Vrabel responded. Patriots' receiver depth could once again be tested Per MassLive, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III could also be given opportunities to step up if Brown doesn't play this weekend. away.headline: New Patriots rumors update Christian Barmore's availability at NFL trade deadline
away.blurb: New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore is reportedly available as the Nov. 10 trade deadline nears, per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated. "The Patriots are deep in the AFC race, but veteran DT Christian Barmore could be had, having played only 41.9 percent of the team's defensive snaps, falling behind Milton Williams and Cory Durden in the team's rotation." New England selected Barmore with a second round pick (No. 38 overall) in the 2021 NFL draft. He's played 71 games (28 starts) over five-plus seasons. Barmore's best season was 2023, when the former Alabama star amassed 8.5 sacks, 64 tackles (39 solo) and 16 quarterback hits. In April 2024, Barmore signed a four-year, $84 million contract extension, per Over the Cap . Unfortunately, Barmore was diagnosed with blood clots in July 2024, and he ultimately played just four games the following season. He returned to the field in 2025 and became a full-time starter for the first time in his career. Over 17 games (16 starts), Barmore had 29 tackles, 11 quarterback hits and two sacks. Barmore has been productive getting to the quarterback through six games (three sacks). Pats analyst Carlos A. Lopez spoke more on his pass-rushing skills. However, Barmore has seen his playing time dip down from 65 percent of the defensive snaps in 2025, per Pro Football Reference . He has started just one of six games. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about that in a recent press conference. We'll see if Barmore sticks around with the Pats after the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but in the meantime, New England is visiting Miami to play the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

away.headline: Patriots injury analysis: Pats get a much-needed reprieve in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7 | Pats Pulpit Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A New England Patriots Community Pats Pulpit October 30, 2026 Pats Pulpit Notifications Notifications Sections News Notifications New England Patriots Injuries Analyzing the Patriots’ injury situation before their upcoming game against the Dolphins. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. The first injury report of the week will be published on Wednesday afternoon, and give more information about the current state of the team. home.blurb: Only two players on the active roster missed the first practice ahead of the team's Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, but both rookie guard Kadyn Proctor and cornerback JuJu Brents were out because they're in the concussion protocol. The injury report, though, featured eight players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Only Trader had an injury reported in the press box Sunday, so it's possible than any of the other four were injured in practice. The most prominent players among those who were limited were wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot). How the Dolphins' Injury Status Shapes Up Coming Out of the Bye If the Miami Dolphins are going to make it two in a row after getting their first victory of the season, they might have to overcome some injury issues. Hafley also indicated that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. home.headline: Dolphins get possible break before showdown with red-hot Drake Maye
home.blurb: Star receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday’s matchup after missing the past two practices. Brown’s knee issue flared up this week, sources told NFL Network. He was limited in Wednesday’s practice before sitting out the next two sessions. The injury report also listed an ankle injury, which forced him onto injured reserve after the Patriots’ season opener. The Miami Dolphins could catch a major break Sunday if one of the New England Patriots’ biggest offensive weapons can’t take the field. If Brown is sidelined, New England will be dangerously thin at wide receiver, with DeMario “Pop” Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III as the only healthy receivers on the 53-man roster. That would be welcome news for a Miami secondary that struggled in last weekend’s win against the New York Jets. Geno Smith torched the Dolphins for 287 passing yards and three touchdowns. Still, Miami faces another major challenge. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has thrown for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions over his last four games, leading New England to a 2-2 record during that stretch. Containing Maye will require a complete defensive effort, according to Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley. “It’s going to take all 11,” Hafley said. “I mean, just like playing any guy who can scramble, we’re going to have to be really good up front in our rush lanes. We can’t rush too high. All of our pressures, we got to be careful because, say, you’re overloading one side and you have no contain to the other, you got to be careful. “He’s done a really good job. His off-schedule plays, just watching them, they’re as good as anyone that I’ve seen around the league up to this point, in the six games that we’ve had. But he’s a good player, and he’s big, and he’s physical. I mean, he’s not a guy that’s going to slide. He’s going to try to stiff-arm guys. So I really have a ton of respect for the way he plays the game.” Brown’s potential absence would certainly help Miami, but the Dolphins can’t afford to take their eyes off Maye. Even without a full complement of receivers, New England’s quarterback has shown he can make defenses pay — and Miami’s secondary has already had enough trouble stopping the pass.

home.headline: AJ Brown questionable for Patriots' game at Dolphins due to worrisome knee issue
home.blurb: While speaking with reporters on Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Brown "is questionable" for this coming Sunday's game between 4-3 New England and the 1-5 Miami Dolphins at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium. Could A.J. Brown be a game-time decision for Dolphins game? As Rodney Knuppel of NESN pointed out, the Patriots were already set to be without receivers Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins before Brown missed multiple practices this week. Thus, fourth-year pro DeMario Douglas could end up being the favorite target of quarterback Drake Maye against the Dolphins. Christian Watson details gritty return to Packers' 'TNF' win over Panthers after breaking rib, spitting up blood A familiar issue popped up on the New England Patriots ' injury report when it was learned earlier in the week that wide receiver A.J. Brown wasn't practicing due to a knee injury. "We'll see how he comes in tomorrow, and then we'll make a decision," Vrabel said about Brown, per Greg A. Bedard of Boston Sports Journal. Brown's history of dealing with what has been referred to as a " degenerative knee condition " is well-known among members of the NFL community. It was reported this past spring that the Los Angeles Rams passed on attempting to acquire Brown because they allegedly didn't want to match the Philadelphia Eagles ' asking price for his services due to concerns related to his knee. More recently, Brown suggested he still wasn't 100 percent in his ongoing recovery from the high ankle sprain he suffered in the Patriots' 13-10 season-opening loss at the Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 9. Brown returned to the lineup on Oct. 18, and he tallied six catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns on 16 targets over his first two games back. Bedard noted that Vrabel was asked on Friday whether the Patriots may have rushed Brown back from the ankle injury. "I don't think those things are really ... I think those are separate issues here," Vrabel responded. Patriots' receiver depth could once again be tested Per MassLive, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III could also be given opportunities to step up if Brown doesn't play this weekend. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions in the Commanders' Showdown With the Eagles, Starting With Jayden Daniels - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Nishant Gupta Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders get their rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, and very little about it looks like the opener. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sept. 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles (52) gets the tackle and forces a fumble by Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. picks.headline: Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy
picks.blurb: Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Nov 10, 2024; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn (L) congratulates Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) after a touchdown drive against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Brandon Lee Gowton Fri, October 30, 2026 at 4:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The amicable Andrew Y kindly kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. 1 – In our Q&A exchange ahead of Week 1 , you said that the Commanders are " one of the most boom-bust teams in the NFL." There's clearly been more bust than boom so far. What's the biggest reason why? In short, I would say: injuries, two rookie coordinators figuring out how to call plays, and poor preparation and in-game decision making that I mostly blame on HC Dan Quinn. I should also throw in that GM Adam Peters deserves some blame for botching the Center situation in the offseason by starting week 1 with career backup IOL Nick Allegretti as our starting Center. On the plus side for Peters, he found a serviceable Center off the scrapheap in Lucas Patrick who has started at Center since week 3. In terms of injuries, the Commanders' week 5 injury report had 23 players on it. I don't remember seeing another injury report that long! Many of those players are on the mend and likely to play this week, but some key remaining absences are LT Laremy Tunsil (out for the year), RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (the best pure rusher on the roster), WR Terry McLaurin (torn patellar tendon, may never be the same player again), and DT Javon Kinlaw (one of our better penetrating IDL). In terms of the coordinators, we knew it was going to be risky having two coordinators who have never called plays in the NFL before and that is bearing out. On defense, DC Daronte Jones is trying to implement the complicated and almost unique Brian Flores defense from Minnesota. The defense is difficult to implement because it requires players to be very versatile, with even DTs occasionally dropping into coverage and CBs blitzing the QB. Even in Minnesota, the Flores defense was ranked 16th in yards allowed in its first two years before being ranked 3rd last year and 1st this year, and I think a lot of the improvement is due to players getting better at understanding their responsibilities. In addition, Daronte Jones is a first-time NFL playcaller and I think is showing a bit of slowness in adapting to mid-game changes by the opposing offense. On the other side of the ball, OC David Blough is a first-time playcaller with only two years of coaching experience and it's occasionally showing. He has a good playbook, but plays are taking too long to get called, players are taking too long to get set, and Blough hasn't been adapting well enough to blitzes by building hot routes into his plays. In terms of Dan Quinn, it's a lot. Even though the Commanders are somewhat middle-of-the-road in terms of number of penalties, they are exceptional at getting penalties that erase big plays. The Commanders have the most yards erased by penalty in the NFL right now, and I think that comes down to coaching and ultimately, Dan Quinn. In addition, Quinn's in-game decisions have cost this team games. If he had called for a field goal on the last play in overtime against the Giants, it's almost certain the Commanders would have won that game. Most importantly though, he's supposed to be a defensive head coach, yet the Commanders defense has been atrocious the entire time he's been here. The defense is better under Jones, but it's still the 9th worst defense in terms of points allowed. 2 – The Commanders decided not to fire Dan Quinn during their bye. How much longer do you think he has left? Reports have been pretty unanimous that owner Josh Harris would rather not fire a coach mid-season, so I think Dan Quinn should be safe until the end of the season unless it looks like the team has quit on him (which it hasn't). For all his other faults, Quinn has traditionally been great at maintaining the locker room and keeping players motivated, so I don't think they're likely to quit on him. At the same time, I think the team would have to not only win the division, but also win a playoff game to keep Quinn around until next year. So I think the most likely outcome is that Quinn gets fired at the end of the season. 3 – Should Washington sign Jayden Daniels to a contract extension this offseason? Will they? Yes and yes. Although Jayden has made a few high-profile gaffes in situational awareness in recent games, he's the biggest reason the Commanders are in those games to begin with. He's adapted to a new (very different) offense really well and is playing from the pocket and even protecting himself better with his choices. He's showing the passing ability you would want from a QB and is an amazing scrambler to boot. My only major concern with Jayden is whether or not he can stay healthy. However, he missed very few games in college and almost all of his games missed in the NFL (both last year and this year) have been due to his left elbow. I'm hoping he has just had a bit of a complicated left elbow problem that will ultimately get fixed. From what I understand, the ligaments in his left elbow may not have healed from last year, which is a low-probability, but very real risk whenever someone dislocates their elbow. It can be fixed with a replacement of damaged or torn ligaments with cadaver ligaments, which I expect Jayden to get after the season is over. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Commanders' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? In terms of favorable matchups, WR Antonio Williams won his matchups against CB Cooper DeJean in week 1, so I expect that matchup to get exploited again. The Commanders also did a pretty good job in week 1 of limiting the Eagles run game outside of Jalen Hurts scrambles and I expect them to do it again. The Daronte Jones/Brian Flores scheme is particularly good at stopping the run. The biggest matchup against the Commanders is probably the Eagles DL against the Commanders run game. The Commanders have not been able to move the ball effectively on the ground outside of Jayden Daniels' scrambles. I think the issue is partly run blocking, partly abandoning the run in playcalling, and partly that very little capital has been invested in the RB room. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Commanders currently listed as 5.5-point home favorites, what's your score prediction? Maybe 23-17 in favor of the Commanders. In Week 1 when these teams played, the Eagles offense relied heavily on Jalen Hurts scrambles to move the ball in critical situations. Tanner McKee doesn't seem to have the same scrambling ability. The Commanders also let in a lot of interior pressure in that matchup with Nick Allegretti playing at Center. With Lucas Patrick there now, the pass protection should be improved.

The injury occurred during a team drill on a day that is considered a light practice. He'll undergo more tests Saturday, but initial X-rays showed significant damage, a team source told ESPN. Depending on what the additional tests reveal, it's possible Payne, who's in the final year of his contract, will be done for the season. It's yet another blow for the Commanders, who are 1-4-1 in a pivotal third season for coach Dan Quinn. They also will be without their other starting defensive end, Javon Kinlaw, for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) because of a knee injury. Payne has been a longtime starter along Washington's defensive line since the organization drafted him with the No. 13 pick in 2018. He's their longest-tenured position player. He started every game between 2020 and 2024, missed only two games last season and has started every one this year. Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 after recording a career-best 11.5 sacks. He's had a combined 11 sacks since that season and that was the only year he topped five. But his strength has been playing the run. Earlier Friday, Quinn said he valued Payne's "strength inside, his power, and oftentimes that's where he wins on whether it's pass rush or [tackles for a loss]. But some of the dirty work doesn't go in a stat, but you can definitely feel it." Washington does have depth at defensive end with Deatrich Wise Jr. and Charles Omenihu. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Daron Payne Injured, Latest NFL Rumors on Commanders DT's Status and Return Timeline Amid Foot Issue
home.blurb: Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne will "likely" head to injured reserve after suffering a "significant" foot injury, per Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Payne has played all nine of his NFL seasons with Washington, which selected the former Alabama star with the 13th overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft. He's started six games this season and amassed 14 tackles (seven solo), five quarterback hits and one sack. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.
